title: Lament over Pharaoh and Egypt
description:
In the twelfth year Ezekiel is commanded to chant a lament over Pharaoh, king of Egypt.  
Pharaoh is compared to a young lion among the nations and to a sea monster in the waters that stirs up the seas with its feet.  
The Lord will cast His net over him, draw him up, and throw him onto dry land, where birds and wild animals will feed on him.  
His flesh will be scattered across the mountains, and his blood will water the earth.  
The heavens will grow dark, the stars will lose their light, and the kings of the nations will tremble when the king of Babylon comes with a sword against Egypt.  
The land will be laid waste, and the daughters of the nations will sing a lament over the fall of Egypt.
